God doth not require of people things not in their power; yet bare velleities, or pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tended willings are not accepted: there must be an acting ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cording to our power to justifie the sincerity of our willing mind; and men vainly pretend to will that towards the perfor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mance of which they never move. Though God requireth not of us things that are not within our power, yet he requireth of us the putting forth of our power in doing what he hath com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />manded us, so far as we are able; which indeed can alone justi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fie the willingness of our mind to be more than a mere pretence. A present impotency, if contracted by our own fault, will not excuse us from the performance of those Acts as to which it doth extend, to which some are bound by the just Laws of God or men: but it is very unreasonable to think, it should excuse as to those Acts to which it doth not extend, and as to which it cannot be pleaded.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 For <ns0:hi>I mean</ns0:hi> not that other men be eased, and you burdened <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">I do not press you to such proportions in giving as should make your afflicted Brethren rich, and you poor.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 But by an equality <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">But only to bring you and them to some equality, that they might not starve, while you have plenty, and what you may well enough spare.</ns0:note>: <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> now at this time your abundance <ns0:hi>may be a supply</ns0:hi> for their want <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">I do not urge you to make your necessaries a supply for others wants. I would only have a supply for their wants out of your abundance.</ns0:note>, that their abundance may be also <ns0:hi>a supply</ns0:hi> for your want <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>That their abundance may al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />so be a supply for your want</ns0:hi>: Some by their <ns0:hi>abundance</ns0:hi> understand their aboundings in the good things of this life: They are now in distress by reason of the great Famine that is in <ns0:hi>Iudea,</ns0:hi> or by reason of the great storm of persecution that is there raised a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gainst Christians; yet God may turn the Scales, he may send a Famine in those parts where you live, and there may be plenty in <ns0:hi>Iudea</ns0:hi>; then their abundance may supply your wants. O<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers interpret <ns0:hi>their abundance,</ns0:hi> of the aboundings of their Grace, which may quicken them up to pray for you, for the supply of such Grace to you as you stand in need of.</ns0:note>, that there may be equality <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">That so there may be an equality, they being Instruments of Spiritual Blessings to you, as you are Instruments of temporal Blessings and good things to them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 As it is written, He that <ns0:hi>had gathered</ns0:hi> much, had nothing over; and he that <ns0:hi>had gathered</ns0:hi> little, had no lack <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">This Quotation would incline us to think, that the <ns0:hi>abun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dance</ns0:hi> mentioned in the latter part of the former Verse, as also the <ns0:hi>equality</ns0:hi> mentioned in the end of it, is rather to be under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stood with reference to the good things of this life, than with reference to <ns0:hi>Spiritual Blessings</ns0:hi>; or to temporal, and spiritual put together, balancing one another to make an equality. For cer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tain it is, that this Quotation referreth to <ns0:hi>Manna,</ns0:hi> which was the Bread God afforded for the Bodies of his people in the Wil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derness, though considered <ns0:hi>typically</ns0:hi> it is rightly by the Apostle called <ns0:hi>spiritual bread,</ns0:hi> 1 Cor. 10.5. signifying that Bread which came down from Heaven, which <ns0:hi>Moses could not give</ns0:hi> (as Christ tells us, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 6.50, 58.) These words are quoted from <ns0:hi>Ex.</ns0:hi> 16.18, though more agreeably to the <ns0:hi>Septuagint</ns0:hi> than to our translation. The History is this. The <ns0:hi>Manna</ns0:hi> being fallen, the Text saith <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 17. <ns0:hi>that some gathered more, some less</ns0:hi>; but it so fell out, by the Providence of God ordering it, that when they came, and measured what they had gathered, <ns0:hi>He that gathered much had nothing over, and he that gathered little had no lack.</ns0:hi> Now of this the Apostle makes an Argument to press the <ns0:hi>Corinthians</ns0:hi> to this charitable Act. The force of which lies in this. As it was in the case of <ns0:hi>Manna</ns0:hi>; there were some that gathered more, o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers that gathered less, yet all had enough; So it will be as to the riches of the World that men gather, though some gather more, and others gather less, yet men will find, that those that have <ns0:hi>gathered little</ns0:hi> (have less Estates than others) using what they have to the glory of God, and according to the divine rule, will have no lack: And those that have gathered much, if they do not distribute it according to the will of God, will find that they have nothing over; God will shrink their heap into some equality to those whom at Gods command they would not re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieve, Eccl. 5.10. <ns0:hi>He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with sil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ver.</ns0:hi> The wisdom of the Divine Providence, hath not ordained <ns0:hi>levelling,</ns0:hi> nor made all men equal in their portions of the good things of this life; but he hath willed such an <ns0:hi>equality</ns0:hi> as every one may eat, (unless he or she that will not work) either from the sweat of their own faces, or from the charity of others. Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sides, nature craveth no great things, but is satisfied with a little; So as he that hath gathered little shall have no lack, if he can but moderate the excesses of his Appetite. And he that hath ga<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thered much hath <ns0:hi>nothing over,</ns0:hi> what is either necessary for him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self and his Family, or what he ought to part with for the re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lief of others at the Command of God.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:468" />16 But thanks <ns0:hi>be</ns0:hi> to God, which put the same earnest care into the heart of Titus for you.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 For indeed he accepted the exhortation, but being more forward, of his own accord he went unto you <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">The Apostle, by his Exhortation, put <ns0:hi>Titus</ns0:hi> upon this em<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ployment of making at <ns0:hi>Corinth</ns0:hi> an extraordinary Collection for the poor Christians that were in <ns0:hi>Iudea</ns0:hi>; but it should seem, that when he did it, <ns0:hi>Titus</ns0:hi> let him know, that he was before resolved upon it: so as, though he went at the entreaty of the Apostle, yet he went also of his own accord, having resolved upon the work before the Apostle spoke to him of it.                   </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 And we have sent with him the brother, whose praise <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> in the gospel, throughout all the churches <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Who this other Brother was, whether <ns0:hi>Luke,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Barnabas,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Silas,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Apollos,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Mark,</ns0:hi> is not much material; it is plain, whoever he was, that he was a <ns0:hi>Brother</ns0:hi> and a <ns0:hi>Minister,</ns0:hi> one who had a good repute for preaching the Gospel.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 And not <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> only, but who was also chosen of the churches to travel with us, with this <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>gift.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> grace <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">And that he was chosen by the Churches to go along with <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Titus,</ns0:hi> to carry the Charity of other Churches to the distressed Christians in <ns0:hi>Iudea</ns0:hi>; which Charity is here again cal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />led <ns0:hi>Grace,</ns0:hi> for the reason before mentioned, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 1.</ns0:note> which is administred by us to the glory of the same Lord, and <ns0:hi>declaration</ns0:hi> of your ready mind <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">He de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />clares that their end in this Administration, was the Glory of God, and the proof and declaration of these <ns0:hi>Corinthians</ns0:hi> since<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rity of <ns0:hi>brotherly Love,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>ready mind</ns0:hi> to yield obedience to the Will of God declared to them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 Avoiding this, that no man should blame us in this abundance which is administred by us <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">I have sent more than one as witnesses of what is done in this Service, that none might reflect upon those trusted with the Charity of divers Churches, as if they converted any part of it to their own private use, and did not distribute it to those for whom it was given. The Apostle here commendeth to all Mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nisters and Christians, a prudent foresight of such scandalous imputations, as they may be exposed to (be their sincerity what it will) from the men of the world, who have no good will to<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wards them, and a provision against them. <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> could have trusted <ns0:hi>Titus</ns0:hi> in the distribution of these Alms, but he did not know what the World might say, had he discharged the trust alone; he therefore takes in one with him, to be a witness of his actions.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Pet. 2.12.</ns0:note> Providing for honest things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">He had said the same <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 12.17. In both places he in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />structeth us, what is the great Duty of all Christians, but of Ministers especially, (who are as Cities built upon an Hill, and cannot be hid, and against whom ill men are much more ready to open their mouths, than against private Christians of a more obscure condition) <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Provide things honest, not only in the sight of God,</ns0:hi> (having an eye, that in our actions we do nothing which God hath forbidden us, nor omit any thing which God hath commanded us) but also looking that in our conversation we (as much as in us lies) do those things which have a good report amongst men, <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 4.8.                         </ns0:gap>tus,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Apollos,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Softhenes,</ns0:hi> or any other; it is sufficient for us to know, that he was a <ns0:hi>Brother,</ns0:hi> and one of whose diligence and faithfulness the Apostle and the Churches, where <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> now was, had had ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />perience.</ns0:note>, whom we have oftentimes proved diligent in many things, but now much more diligent upon the great confidence which <ns0:note place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>he hath.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:hi>I have</ns0:hi> in you <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">And that he was now very ready and forward to be imployed in this Service, upon the Apostles recommenda<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of this Church unto him.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 Whether <ns0:hi>any do inquire</ns0:hi> of Titus, <ns0:hi>he is</ns0:hi> my partner and fellow-helper concerning you: or our brethren <ns0:hi>be inquired of, they are</ns0:hi> the messengers of the churches <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">This Verse contains the Apostles credential Letters, given to <ns0:hi>Titus,</ns0:hi> and the other two persons, sent about the business of making this Collection in the Church of <ns0:hi>Corinth.</ns0:hi> Many, in mat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ters where the drawing of their purses is sollicited and concer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ned, are very scrupulous and inquisitive, seeking all advantages to excuse themselves; one while pleading their own poverty, another while objecting against the state, or want, or quality of those for whom they are sollicited; again, questioning, whe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther their <ns0:hi>Charity</ns0:hi> shall ever come to those persons for whom it is desired, objecting against the persons intrusted with the con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />veyance or distribution of it. The Apostle having therefore before obviated some Objections, he here obviateth the last mentioned, letting them know, that the persons intrusted with this Service, were unexceptionable persons. He calleth <ns0:hi>Titus</ns0:hi> his <ns0:hi>Partner and Fellow-helper concerning them,</ns0:hi> that is, in the busi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness of the Gospel, and promoting the Salvation of their Souls. For the others, he tells them they were such as the Churches had thought fit to make their Messengers; so had the credit of the Churches, whose Messengers they were, who would not have intrusted them, if they had not judged them faithful.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> the glory of Christ <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">He either calleth the Churches, or them, <ns0:hi>the Glory of Christ.</ns0:hi> If the words be to be understood of the <ns0:hi>Messengers,</ns0:hi> (which seemeth the fairest application of them) the meaning is, that they were Instruments of the glory of Christ; or persons who, by their Grace, did bring much glory to Christ. Every one that excelleth in the habits or exercise of Grace, is the glory of Christ, because without Christ he can do nothing of that nature: <ns0:hi>I live, yet not I, but Christ liveth in me.</ns0:hi> The acts and exercises of Grace are indeed our acts, but the power by which we do them, is from Christ; we glory in Christ, and by our holy con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />versations glorifie Christ, and Christ glorieth in every pious and holy person, as God did concerning <ns0:hi>Iob, Chap.</ns0:hi> 1.8. & 2.3.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 Wherefore shew ye to them, and before the churches, the proof of your love, and of our boast<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing on your behalf <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">The Chapter concludeth with an Exhortation to their li<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />berallty, backed with an heap of Arguments. 1. It would be an evidence of their love to God, to their afflicted Brethren, and to the Apostle. 2. It would be a proof of it to those Messen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gers of the Churches, and to the Churches whose Messengers they were. 3.
